paper.title: Agentic Proof and Property-Based Testing via Property-Templates in Data-Intensive Computing

summary.text: A study of recurring correctness properties in Apache Spark, expressed as parameterised property templates with holes. The authors use the templates in a dual-track framework that both proves properties in the Lean 4 theorem prover and instantiates them as executable PySpark property-based tests. They report that templates raise agentic proof success by up to 2.6x, cut proof hallucinations by 59%, and reduce intent misalignments in synthesised tests from 22 to 1.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Testing for data-intensive systems rather than for DBMSs, and the work is not built on SQLancer; the abstract compares against a Spark fuzzer, not against SQLancer.
supporting_excerpts: We design an agentic, dual-track validation framework that uses property templates to formally verify correctness in the Lean 4 theorem prover and instantiate PBT templates as executable PySpark tests.
Template-guided synthesis further exceeds a state-of-the-art Spark fuzzer and approaches unguided LLM-based PBT on code coverage.
